assertions.name: offdiagonal_gram_still_does_not_separate
assertions.source: active same True, duals same True

description: EXPLORATORY (bean t7qv): builds the H_{3A} Frobenius Gram WITH off-diagonals and settles what it does and does not fix. In the BLOCK basis diagonality is a theorem (central idempotents are orthogonal), so off-diagonals exist only away from the centre; the right object is the Gram on the constituent subalgebra (H_3)^(x)A < H_{3A}, dimension 6^A. Markov trace multiplicativity on disjoint strand blocks is verified (max rel err 1.1e-8, the f64 y_lambda precision), giving G^(A) = G^(x)A with rank exactly 5^A and radical 6^A - 5^A (1, 11, 91, 671 for A=1..4). BUT it does not unblock Phase B: because b_1 = 1, G_{1j} = t_j, i.e. t = G e_1, so row 1 of `Gx >= u` IS the objective, it is always the binding row, the optimum is always u_1 and the dual is always e_1 — measured invariant across equality/inequality forms, realisable/non-realisable/kernel demands, identity kept or dropped, and T vs He3 (identical active sets AND duals, only the objective differing). This unifies prop:operator-selection-lp's two documented degeneracies with the two measured, and WITHDRAWS the previous turn's 'the blocker is the diagonal Gram', which was a special case. No fit; nothing wired.
caveats: The BLOCK-basis Gram of nucleus_sdp_assembly is diagonal by a theorem — central primitive idempotents are orthogonal, so tr_M(P_l P_m) = delta tr_M(P_l) identically. Nothing was 'omitted' there and nothing can be added. The Gram built here is a different object on a different space, the constituent subalgebra, and does not replace it.

G^(A) = G^(x)A rests on Markov multiplicativity across disjoint strand blocks, verified to 1.1e-8 relative — the precision of the stored f64 y_lambda table, not an exact check. An exact verification wants a higher-precision y_lambda source.

The A5 sweep is at A=2 (dim 36) for cost; A6 confirms the same dual degeneracy at A=3 (dim 216). Box bounds +-1e4 are used to keep the LP bounded; with the identity dropped from the basis the LP becomes unbounded and hits them, which is reported as a failed route rather than a result.
